findings.title: Machine-readable report contract is not lossless
findings.claim: REPORT-CONTRACT.md declares claim and mechanism mandatory for every material finding, but the canonical machine-readable JSON example omits both fields.
findings.mechanism: An auditor following the canonical JSON example can produce a structurally plausible object that loses the semantic proposition and causal explanation required by the same contract, forcing downstream intake to reinterpret prose.
findings.expected_behavior: Every mandatory load-bearing finding field is represented in the machine-readable contract or an explicitly lossless equivalent.
findings.observed_behavior: The prose required-field list includes claim and mechanism while the canonical JSON example omits both.
findings.reproducer: Compare AUDIT-METHODOLOGY/REPORT-CONTRACT.md sections 'Required finding fields' and 'Machine-readable block' at target commit efecb86326a5935d0996cf4f3f1ba21b8106890d.
findings.consequence: External-audit ingestion can be lossy and can silently reinterpret the auditor's claim or mechanism.
findings.close_variant_result: No fixed-count or quantity-gaming contradiction was reproduced; the defect is specific to required-field parity between prose and machine-readable output.
findings.proposed_change: Add claim and mechanism to the canonical machine-readable finding object, publish a matching JSON Schema, and regression-test required-field parity.

findings.title: Untrusted target data can become executable authority through baseline discovery
findings.claim: The methodology declares target repository content untrusted data but later permits target-shipped tests/checkers and requires baseline discovery from target-controlled CI, README, and helpers without one universal pre-execution safety gate.
findings.mechanism: A compromised or adversarial target can place executable commands in target-controlled baseline surfaces. A literal auditor can execute those commands as the discovered baseline, converting target data into action authority unless an independent sandbox and inspection rule intervenes.
findings.expected_behavior: Target content may suggest candidate commands, but every target-derived execution is inspected and run only in a constrained disposable environment unless separately authorized by the control plane.
findings.observed_behavior: The prompt establishes a universal untrusted-data rule but provides broad target-derived execution authority, while the explicit outside-write inspection warning is scoped only to legacy helpers.
findings.reproducer: Read AUDIT-METHODOLOGY/CANONICAL-AGENT-AUDIT-PROMPT.md sections '0. CONTROL PLANE / UNTRUSTED TARGET BOUNDARY', '2. SAFETY / MUTATION BOUNDARY', and '7. DISCOVER THE BASELINE, THEN RUN IT' at the resolved target commit and compare their authority rules.
findings.consequence: An execution-capable auditor can be induced to run target-defined code or violate the methodology's own read-only and no-external-side-effect boundaries.
findings.close_variant_result: Target-mode resolution and blindness boundaries were not contradicted; the defect is specifically the transition from untrusted target text to executable baseline authority.
findings.proposed_change: Add a universal TARGET-DERIVED EXECUTION GATE covering tests, checkers, package hooks, build steps, liveness scripts, and helpers: inspect first, remove credentials, constrain filesystem/network, and require separate authority for external effects.

findings.title: Behavioral A/B protocol lacks explicit state isolation or reset
findings.claim: The behavioral A/B protocol randomizes conditions and keeps runtime factors constant but does not mandate fresh sessions/processes or equivalent reset of persistent memory, cache, tool state, conversation history, and writable fixtures.
findings.mechanism: In a normal stateful agent, one condition can alter state consumed by a later condition. Randomization does not eliminate carryover, so treatment leakage can bias the estimated AHP effect.
findings.expected_behavior: Each condition begins from an explicitly equivalent clean state, or a defined crossover/washout design records and controls residual shared state.
findings.observed_behavior: The protocol specifies same agent/runtime, constant factors, randomization, and blinding but no mandatory state-reset or session-isolation clause.
findings.reproducer: Inspect AUDIT-METHODOLOGY/BEHAVIORAL-EVALUATION-PROTOCOL.md sections 'Experimental conditions', 'Blinding', 'Unit of analysis', and 'Acceptance criteria' and verify that no mandatory reset/isolation rule is present.
findings.consequence: Behavioral evaluation can attribute persistent-state carryover to AHP benefit or harm, reducing causal validity even when scoring is blinded.
findings.close_variant_result: Randomization and blinding are present and were not rejected; they are insufficient by themselves to remove state carryover.
findings.proposed_change: Require fresh process/session or snapshot/restore between conditions, reset persistent state and writable fixtures, record unavoidable shared state, and define crossover/washout handling.
